The '''2012–13 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 111th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 81st in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the 3rd since its organization under a league committee separate from [[Serie B]]. It began on 25 August 2012 and ended on 19 May 2013.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/17077/no-early-serie-start |publisher=[[Football Italia]]| work=Football-Italia.net| date=26 March 2012 |title=No early Serie A start}}</ref> [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] were the defending champions.

A total of 20 teams contested the league, comprising 17 sides from the [[2011–12 Serie A|2011–12 season]] and three promoted from the [[2011–12 Serie B]]. As in the previous years, [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] provided the official ball for all matches, with a new Nike Maxim Serie A model to be used throughout the season for all matches.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nike MAXIM, La Liga and Serie A 2012/13 balls|url=http://pes-parche.com/2012/03/balones-nike-maxim-temporada-2012-2013-official-match-ball-full-hd.html|publisher=pes-parche.com|date=20 April 2012|access-date=20 April 2012|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402171039/http://pes-parche.com/2012/03/balones-nike-maxim-temporada-2012-2013-official-match-ball-full-hd.html|archive-date=2 April 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 21 August 2012, [[FIGC]] allowed Serie A teams to have up to 12 substitution players on the bench for each game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/33240/2012/08/News.shtml |title = Figc {{!}} News - La Figc autorizza la 'panchina lunga' con 12 giocatori  |access-date=7 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208004920/http://www.figc.it/it/204/33240/2012/08/News.shtml |archive-date=8 February 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/85.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_33258_StrilloComunicatoUfficiale_lstAllegati_Allegato_0_upfAllegato.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=7 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304141224/http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/85.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_33258_StrilloComunicatoUfficiale_lstAllegati_Allegato_0_upfAllegato.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Events==
The 2012–13 season features the return of [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]], [[Torino F.C.|Torino]], and [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], who were promoted back to Serie A after nineteen, three, and one years respectively. It is also [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]]'s first season out of [[Stadio Sant'Elia]] after more than 40 years, following its closure due to safety issues; as a replacement, the team agreed to renovate the [[Stadio Is Arenas]] located in [[Quartu Sant'Elena]], in order to use it as its home venue for this season (Cagliari has ongoing plans to build its own brand-new stadium in the next few years).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/cagliari/2012/05/21/news/rivoluzione_in_arrivo_is_arenas-35653028/ |publisher=La Repubblica |language=it |access-date=21 May 2012 |date=21 May 2012 |title=Sant'Elia addio, 'Is Arenas' è realtà}}</ref> The fixtures were presented on 26 July in a lavish hour-long televised ceremony.

===Scoring===
* First goal of the season: [[Maicosuel]] for Udinese against Fiorentina (<small>''25 August 2012''</small>)
* Fastest goal of the season: '''18 seconds'''
** [[Arturo Vidal]] for Juventus against Internazionale (<small>''3 November 2012''</small>)
* Latest goal of the season: '''90+5 minutes'''
** [[Panagiotis Kone]] for Bologna against Catania (<small>''30 September 2012''</small>)
** [[Josip Iličić]] for Palermo against Catania (<small>''21 April 2013''</small>)
* Largest winning margin: '''6 goals'''<ref name="stats">{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/stats?league=ita.1&year=2012|title=Italian Serie A Statistics – 2012–13|work=ESPN|publisher=Entertainment and Sports Programming Network|access-date=25 August 2012}}</ref>
** Sampdoria 6–0 Pescara (<small>''27 January 2013''</small>)
** Lazio 6–0 Bologna (<small>''5 May 2013''</small>)
* Highest scoring game: '''8 goals'''<ref name="stats" />
** Torino 3–5 Napoli (<small>''30 March 2013''</small>)
* Most goals scored by a single team: '''6 goals'''<ref name="stats" />
** Pescara 1–6 Juventus (<small>''10 November 2012''</small>)
** Sampdoria 6–0 Pescara (<small>''27 January 2013''</small>)
** Lazio 6–0 Bologna (<small>''5 May 2013''</small>)
* Most goals scored by a losing team: '''3 goals'''<ref name="stats" />
** Cagliari 4–3 Torino (<small>''24 February 2013''</small>)
** Torino 3–5 Napoli (<small>''30 March 2013''</small>)
** Internazionale 3–4 Atalanta (<small>''7 April 2013''</small>)
** Fiorentina 4–3 Torino (<small>''21 April 2013''</small>)

===Clean sheets===
* Most [[Shutout|clean sheets]]: '''19'''<ref name="stats" />
** Juventus
* Fewest clean sheets: '''5'''<ref name="stats" />
** Pescara
